findings.reason: Verified in the diff: the size>1 check that threw is removed, DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider and WildFlyElytronProvider all return order 200, so a FIPS deployment that also has the default provider now silently gets whichever ServiceLoader returns first, with only a debug log.

The single default-size EC key is reused for ES256/384/512, so most cases sign on a mismatched curve, and the self-comparison round trip would not catch a truncating integerToBytes, which is a real but non-critical test weakness.
The two ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls at lines 114-115 have discarded results and are dead code, so this is a correct cleanup note with no behavioural impact.

The abstract int order() added to the public CryptoProvider SPI does break external implementers that do not override it, which is a real compatibility concern, but it is phrased as a question and the impact is limited to third-party providers.
